sequence.description: The log's head once the command committed: its last event, or the head it saw when it appended none.

changed.description: False for a command that was accepted and changed nothing, so appended no event.

sequence.description: The log's head when the command was rejected.

reason.description: Why the command was rejected, the code of its error: not_found when its target does not exist.

code.description: A stable error code in snake case.

error.description: The rejection as an error: its code (the reason), a message for people and structured data.

receipt.description: A command's receipt: accepted (with the head sequence after it and whether it changed anything) or rejected (with the reason and the error). A retry with the same commandId answers the same receipt.

result.description: The method's result, present when this request applied the command; absent on a retry and on a rejection.

name.description: A webhook endpoint's name on its environment: 1 to 40 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, unique.

url.description: Where the endpoint's POSTs go: https, or http only to loopback, localhost, a private or tailnet address or a .ts.net name; with no userinfo, and its host off the denylist.

secretKind.description: Where a webhook endpoint's secret is, never the secret: pasted (sent once and kept in the environment's vault), reference (a key-manager reference resolved per delivery) or missing (none, so a delivery to it fails).

at.description: An instant as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

result.description: What a delivery attempt came to: delivered, retrying (it failed and is retried at retryAt: a network error, a timeout, 408, 429 or 5xx) or failed (finally).

status.description: The HTTP status a webhook answered; null for a client notice, or when none came.

error.description: What went wrong; null when it was delivered.

lastResult.description: What the latest POST to it came to, a delivery's or a test's; null before the first.

endpoint.description: A webhook endpoint the environment names for routines to deliver to: its name, URL, where its secret is, and its last result; never the secret.
